title: Attention Heads Hold the Key to Understanding Safety Mechanisms in Large Language Models

problem.claim: LLM safety mechanisms are important for preventing harmful content generation and improving transparency.

gap.claim: The relationship between attention heads and LLM safety is insufficiently understood, limiting fine-grained characterization of safety mechanisms.

contributions.claim: AHSCC detects attention-head safety correlations using representation similarity and verifies causal influence through patch-based intervention.
Safety-related attention heads are distributed across intermediate LLM layers, and intervening on them can control safety behavior.
AHSFT improves LLM safety through lightweight fine-tuning of specific safety-related attention heads.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report finding numerous safety-related attention heads across intermediate layers.
The authors report that direct intervention on these attention heads can significantly control LLM safety behavior.
The authors report that AHSFT further improves LLM safety.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM safety mechanisms help prevent harmful content generation, and mechanistic interpretation supports transparency and safety improvement.
Attention-head involvement in safety is insufficiently understood for complete fine-grained characterization.
AHSCC combines representation-similarity correlation detection with patch-based causal intervention verification.
Safety-related attention heads occur across intermediate layers and can substantially control safety behavior when intervened on.
AHSFT uses lightweight fine-tuning of selected safety-related attention heads to improve safety and transparency.

unknowns: Specific models, datasets, safety tasks, and evaluation metrics are not provided.
The abstract does not report quantitative results or comparison baselines.
The causal verification protocol and fine-tuning configuration are not specified.
